content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Alexander Brown (E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says admin requires owning role (Payroll Specialist) so max is write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says security record governs, contractors max is read without advanced training; admin never allowed.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security note says security record governs. The policy states contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Access levels: none, read, write, admin.

The employee requested admin. Admin is never allowed for contractors. Max per security record is read (basic training). Even under HR record, max is write (Analyst doesn't own Payroll).

Given the security record governs (as noted), the max is read. Requested admin is above max, so grant the maximum = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
